Package : certifi
Version : 2025.11.12
License : Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL 2.0)
URL     : https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi
Shipped : yes
------------------------------------------------------------
This package contains a modified version of ca-bundle.crt:

ca-bundle.crt -- Bundle of CA Root Certificates

This is a bundle of X.509 certificates of public Certificate Authorities
(CA). These were automatically extracted from Mozilla's root certificates
file (certdata.txt).  This file can be found in the mozilla source tree:
https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/file/tip/security/nss/lib/ckfw/builtins/certdata.txt
It contains the certificates in PEM format and therefore
can be directly used with curl / libcurl / php_curl, or with
an Apache+mod_ssl webserver for SSL client authentication.
Just configure this file as the SSLCACertificateFile.#

"Target Code" refers to output from any compiler for a real or virtual

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see https://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see https://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see https://opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
    1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
    1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
    2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
    1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
    2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no
    2.0.1           2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.1           2.1+2.0.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.2           2.1.1       2002        PSF         yes
    2.1.3           2.1.2       2002        PSF         yes
    2.2 and above   2.1.1       2001-now    PSF         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with
    other software that is released under the GPL; the others don't.

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
    because its license has a choice of law clause.  According to
    CNRI, however, Stallman's lawyer has told CNRI's lawyer that 1.6.1
    is "not incompatible" with the GPL.

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.

## About Tauri

Tauri is a polyglot and generic system that is very composable and allows engineers to make a wide variety of applications. It is used for building applications for Desktop Computers using a combination of Rust tools and HTML rendered in a Webview. Apps built with Tauri can ship with any number of pieces of an optional JS API / Rust API so that webviews can control the system via message passing. In fact, developers can extend the default API with their own functionality and bridge the Webview and Rust-based backend easily.

Tauri apps can have custom menus and have tray-type interfaces. They can be updated, and are managed by the user's operating system as expected. They are very small, because they use the system's webview. They do not ship a runtime, since the final binary is compiled from rust. This makes the reversing of Tauri apps not a trivial task.

## This module

This is a typescript library that creates `cjs` and `esm` JavaScript endpoints for you to import into your Frontend framework so that the Webview can call and listen to backend activity. We also ship the pure typescript, because for some frameworks this is more optimal. It uses the message passing of webviews to their hosts.

To learn more about the details of how all of these pieces fit together, please consult this [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md) document.

## Installation

The preferred method is to install this module locally as a dependency:

```
$ pnpm add @tauri-apps/api
$ yarn add @tauri-apps/api
$ npm add @tauri-apps/api
```

## Semver

**tauri** is following [Semantic Versioning 2.0](https://semver.org/).

============================================================
SECTION 6: Bundled Fonts
============================================================

The Whisperstream desktop app bundles two font families locally under
frontend/public/fonts/ and loads them via @font-face rules in
frontend/src/styles/globals.css. No font-CDN requests are made at runtime.

------------------------------------------------------------
Family           : Outfit
Weights          : 300, 400, 500, 600
Source           : https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit
License          : SIL Open Font License 1.1

redistributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The governing terms

============================================================
SECTION 7: Bundled Binary and Downloadable Model Attributions
============================================================

This section covers:
  - llama-server.exe and its runtime DLLs (bundled in the installer)
  - Qwen3-ASR-0.6B INT8 ONNX model (downloaded for speech recognition)
  - Cohere Transcribe INT8 ONNX model (downloaded for speech recognition)
  - Gemma 4 E2B Instruct GGUF model (downloaded on first use)
  - Stream-1 Mini by Whisperstream GGUF model (downloaded for local cleanup)
  - Supertonic 3 TTS voice model (downloaded only if the optional
    voice feature is enabled)
  - Kokoro 82M TTS model and its supporting English frontend data
    (installed models usable in standard builds; new downloads experimental)

------------------------------------------------------------
Component : llama.cpp (llama-server.exe + runtime DLLs)
Holder    : The ggml authors
License   : MIT
Release   : b10537
URL       : https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
------------------------------------------------------------

The llama-server.exe binary and its companion DLLs (ggml.dll,
llama.dll, llama-server-impl.dll, and ggml-cpu-*.dll) are shipped
inside the Whisperstream installer. They are built from the llama.cpp
project, pinned to release b10537. The governing MIT
license terms appear verbatim below.

The Cohere Transcribe INT8 ONNX speech-recognition export is intended
for on-demand download to Whisperstream's model directory and is not
bundled in the installer. The official upstream model is distributed
by Cohere Labs under the Apache License 2.0. Fangjun Kuang published
the compatible four-file payload through a merged k2-fsa release
workflow and an immutable ModelScope Git commit. A separate
Apache-2.0 repository preserves the mel-contract exporter, decoder
exporter, tokenizer generator, and INT8 quantizer used for this model
family. The compatible payload repository itself does not contain a
standalone license or a complete build environment. Lanreal's owner
accepted that narrow intermediary provenance uncertainty for this
exact checksum-pinned payload; this notice does not describe the
artifact as independently attorney-cleared. Modification notice: this
payload is published as an INT8 ONNX conversion and dynamic
quantization of the upstream model, arranged for sherpa-onnx
inference; Lanreal has not independently reproduced the exact
converted bytes. Test WAV files are excluded.

------------------------------------------------------------
Kokoro v1.0 upstream runtime for the GPL source edition

Distributor: Fangjun Kuang (csukuangfj), k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx
Pinned model repository:
https://huggingface.co/csukuangfj/kokoro-multi-lang-v1_0/tree/f7b96bb6bef5c5da4d3aa4f4e0498fbbf62dc78b

The model, tokens, voices.bin and US English lexicon are copied without
modification. The upstream model LICENSE is Apache-2.0. Model metadata
attributes its conversion lineage to thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx and upstream
Kokoro. Conversion MIT notices and training-data attribution are retained
alongside this notice and in the generated third-party notices.

The upstream graph/voice binary contains 54 embeddings. The application
exposes only af_heart, af_bella, af_nicole, af_aoede, af_kore, af_sarah,
am_fenrir, am_michael and am_puck. The complete upstream voice file is
downloaded unchanged; it is not a nine-embedding subset.

The upstream US English lexicon derives from hexgrad/misaki (Apache-2.0).
The compiled eSpeak data is separately licensed; the aggregate model LICENSE
does not supersede those terms. Only en_dict, phondata, phonindex, phontab,
intonations and lang/gmw/en and lang/gmw/en-US are selected. Other language
dictionaries, variants, Jieba and Chinese FSTs are not acquired. The selected
compiled data is used unchanged. eSpeak NG is GPL-3.0-or-later; its complete
GPL text is retained in scripts/license-texts/espeak-ng-gpl-3.0.txt and generated
notices. Native eSpeak/piper component notices appear in Section 2.

These model and language-data files download directly from the pinned upstream
repository and are not bundled in the installer. Exact file hashes and sizes
are recorded in upstream-files.json; source/build mappings are documented in
SOURCE-MATERIALS.md.

NOTICE.txt and the NLTK/G2P attribution describe the older eSpeak-free archive,
which is no longer a new-download source but remains supported for existing
caches.

Component : Legacy Kokoro 82M archive (existing caches only)
License   : Apache-2.0, MIT notices, conservative CC attribution
Bundle    : kokoro-82m-fp32-en-us-2026-07-28
Source    : https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
------------------------------------------------------------

The optional archive contains the Kokoro 82M FP32 ONNX model, nine
American English preset embeddings, two pinned Misaki English
lexicons, a pinned PeterReid neural G2P model exported to ONNX, and
three pinned NLTK English perceptron JSON data files. Whisperstream
uses its own modified, inference-only frontend and the ONNX Runtime
already distributed with the application.

Whisperstream does not distribute the Misaki, NLTK, kokoro-onnx,
Torch, Transformers, spaCy, eSpeak, phonemizer, Piper, or num2words
runtime packages in this archive. Exact source pins, modifications,
and the absence of upstream Apache NOTICE files are recorded below.
The nine presets are: af_heart, af_bella, af_nicole, af_aoede,
af_kore, af_sarah, am_fenrir, am_michael, and am_puck.
Kokoro is Apache-2.0; Supertonic's OpenRAIL-M terms do not govern
this Kokoro component.

The following historical Kokoro notice describes that archive and
its frontend, not the complete application environment. The official
sherpa-onnx wheels separately contain eSpeak NG and piper-phonemize
native code, attributed in Section 2.

Whisperstream curated Kokoro 82M English voice bundle

This archive is assembled by Whisperstream from separately pinned,
permissively licensed artifacts. It is not the unmodified output of any one
upstream project.

Kokoro 82M model and voices
Copyright and attribution remain with the Kokoro contributors.
License: Apache License 2.0
Pinned source model:
https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M/tree/f3ff3571791e39611d31c381e3a41a3af07b4987
ONNX release artifacts:
https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases/tag/model-files-v1.0
Modifications: the FP32 ONNX graph is copied unchanged. The upstream voice NPZ
is deterministically reduced to the nine voice presets listed in
export-manifest.json.

ONNX conversion lineage
The pinned thewh1teagle release identifies taylorchu/kokoro-onnx as the source
of the optimized FP32 ONNX graph.
License: MIT
Source: https://github.com/taylorchu/kokoro-onnx
Exact copyright and permission notice:
licenses/TAYLORCHU-KOKORO-ONNX-MIT.txt
The release repository's own exact MIT notice is retained in
licenses/THEWH1TEAGLE-KOKORO-ONNX-MIT.txt. The Kokoro model and voice artifacts
retain their upstream Apache-2.0 license.

Misaki English lexicons
Copyright and attribution remain with the Misaki contributors.
License: Apache License 2.0
Source:
https://github.com/hexgrad/misaki/tree/fba1236595f2d2bf21d414ba6e57d25256afada3
Modifications: only the US gold and silver pronunciation JSON files are
included. Whisperstream does not distribute the Misaki Python package or its
dependency closure.

English neural G2P fallback
Copyright and attribution remain with Peter Reid and contributors.
License: Apache License 2.0
Source:
https://huggingface.co/PeterReid/graphemes_to_phonemes_en_us/tree/a5631b285d18d59483c32c0c3379cb9fac924f4b
Modifications: the pinned BART model is exported to an ONNX forward graph.
The export configuration and output hashes are recorded in
export-manifest.json.

English averaged perceptron tagger data
Original implementation Copyright 2013 Matthew Honnibal.
NLTK modifications Copyright 2015 The NLTK Project.
NLTK port author: Long Duong.
License: MIT
Source:
https://github.com/nltk/nltk_data/tree/550b6625bcef1f2abff2ff770a5a0d272c9c6b2a/packages/taggers
Implementation source:
https://github.com/nltk/nltk/blob/3.9.1/nltk/tag/perceptron.py
Modifications: the three English JSON data files are copied unchanged.
Whisperstream uses a modified, inference-only implementation. Exact copyright
and permission notice: licenses/NLTK-PERCEPTRON-MIT.txt

Conservative training-data attribution
The pinned Kokoro model card identifies Koniwa `tnc` (CC BY 3.0) and SIWIS
(CC BY 4.0) among the shared model's training sources. None of the nine
American English voice presets curated into this archive is a Koniwa or SIWIS
preset. Whisperstream does not redistribute either dataset. Their attribution,
source links, modification statements, and SIWIS citation are retained in
licenses/TRAINING-DATA-ATTRIBUTION.txt.

Apache NOTICE search
No upstream NOTICE text file was found in the pinned Kokoro model snapshot,
Kokoro source repository, Misaki revision, or PeterReid model snapshot. Apache
License 2.0 section 4(d) therefore does not add an upstream NOTICE pass-through
on the reviewed snapshots. The Apache license copy and the modification notices
required by sections 4(a) through 4(c) are preserved.

This archive's inference frontend does not include or invoke eSpeak,
espeak-ng, phonemizer, piper-phonemize, num2words, Torch, Transformers, spaCy,
NLTK, Misaki, or kokoro-onnx. The included data and ONNX graphs are consumed
by Whisperstream's own lightweight frontend and the ONNX Runtime already used
by the app. The current official sherpa runtime separately includes native
eSpeak/Piper components, attributed in Section 2 of the generated third-party
notices.

NLTK averaged perceptron implementation and English model data
------------------------------------------------------------

NLTK averaged perceptron tagger implementation and English model data

Original implementation:
Copyright 2013 Matthew Honnibal

NLTK port and modifications:
Copyright 2015 The NLTK Project
Author: Long Duong

Whisperstream distributes a modified, inference-only implementation and the
three English JSON model-data files. The modified implementation is identified
in src/whisperstream/speech/kokoro_frontend.py.

Conservative Kokoro training-data attribution
------------------------------------------------------------

Conservative Kokoro training-data attribution

Kokoro's pinned model card identifies the following datasets among the inputs
to the shared Kokoro model. The nine American English preset embeddings in the
Whisperstream archive do not include a Koniwa or SIWIS preset. This attribution
is nevertheless retained conservatively because the shared model was trained
in part on these datasets. It does not state or imply that Whisperstream
redistributes either source dataset.

Koniwa `tnc`
Title: Koniwa, an open collection of annotated voices in Japanese language
Audio licensor and attribution party: Television Nishinippon (TNC)
Repository maintainer: shirayu and Koniwa contributors
Source: https://github.com/koniwa/koniwa
Source attribution record: https://github.com/koniwa/koniwa/blob/master/data/tnc/README.md
Audio license identified by the source: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0
License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
Original literary texts: public domain, per the source attribution record
Kokoro model-card use: less than one hour of Japanese training audio
Modification statement: Whisperstream does not distribute or modify the
Koniwa recordings. Kokoro's upstream authors used them while training the
shared Kokoro model.

SIWIS
Title: The SIWIS French Speech Synthesis Database, 2016
Creators: Junichi Yamagishi, Pierre-Edouard Honnet, Philip Garner, and
Alexandros Lazaridis
Publisher: University of Edinburgh, School of Informatics, Centre for Speech
Technology Research
Citation: Yamagishi, Junichi; Honnet, Pierre-Edouard; Garner, Philip;
Lazaridis, Alexandros. (2017). The SIWIS French Speech Synthesis Database,
2016 [dataset]. https://doi.org/10.7488/ds/1705
Source: https://datashare.ed.ac.uk/items/1de74991-eede-4b48-8fbe-6c2abaed88d8
License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Kokoro model-card use: less than eleven hours of French training audio
Modification statement: Whisperstream does not distribute or modify the SIWIS
recordings. Kokoro's upstream authors used them while training the shared
Kokoro model.

No endorsement by the dataset creators, speakers, publishers, or licensors is
stated or implied.
